title: Aray! Health and the body
objectives: Say what hurts with masakit ang... and sumasakit
Describe symptoms: may lagnat, may ubo, may sipon, nahihilo
Handle a pharmacy or clinic visit, including dosage instructions
Describe body positions with naka- statives (nakaupo, nakahiga, nakatayo)

grammar.title: Masakit ang... and may + symptom
grammar.explanation:
The all-purpose pain pattern is masakit ang + body part, with the owner in ng-form: 'Masakit ang ulo ko' — my head hurts (literally: painful the head my). 'Masakit ba ang tiyan mo?' — does your stomach hurt?

For pain that comes and goes, or that started, use the verb sumakit: 'Sumasakit ang likod ko' — my back aches (keeps hurting). 'Sumakit ang tiyan ko kagabi' — my stomach started hurting last night.

For symptoms you HAVE, reach back to A1's may/wala: 'May lagnat ako' — I have a fever. 'May ubo at sipon siya' — he has a cough and a cold. 'Wala na akong lagnat' — my fever is gone. For dizziness and nausea Tagalog prefers verb-like forms: 'Nahihilo ako' — I feel dizzy; 'Nasusuka ako' — I feel like vomiting.

The doctor's opening question is 'Ano po ang nararamdaman ninyo?' — what are you feeling? A good learner answer stacks the patterns: 'Masakit po ang lalamunan ko, at may lagnat po ako.'

examples.tl: Masakit ang ngipin ko. Kailangan ko nang pumunta sa dentista.
examples.en: My tooth hurts. I need to go to the dentist now.

examples.tl: May lagnat ang anak ko mula kagabi.
examples.en: My child has had a fever since last night.

examples.tl: Sumasakit ang mata ko kapag matagal ako sa computer.
examples.en: My eyes hurt when I'm at the computer a long time.

examples.tl: Ano po ang nararamdaman ninyo? — Nahihilo po ako.
examples.en: What are you feeling? — I feel dizzy.

grammar.title: At the pharmacy: dosage and instructions
grammar.explanation:
Pharmacy talk runs on the object-focus verbs you already own. The pharmacist says: 'Inumin ninyo ito tatlong beses sa isang araw' — take (drink) this three times a day. 'Isang tableta pagkatapos kumain' — one tablet after eating. Note that Tagalog 'drinks' medicine — uminom/inumin ng gamot — even for tablets.

Useful structures: X beses sa isang araw (X times a day), bago kumain / pagkatapos kumain (before/after meals), tuwing umaga at gabi (every morning and night), kada anim na oras (every six hours).

Asking for medicine: 'May gamot po ba kayo para sa ubo?' — do you have medicine for a cough? Para sa from Unit 1 returns: gamot para sa lagnat, para sa sakit ng ulo. Some medicines need a prescription: 'Kailangan po ng reseta' — a prescription is needed.

examples.tl: May gamot po ba kayo para sa sipon?
examples.en: Do you have medicine for a cold?

examples.tl: Inumin po ninyo ito dalawang beses sa isang araw, pagkatapos kumain.
examples.en: Take this twice a day, after meals.

examples.tl: Kailangan po ba ng reseta para dito?
examples.en: Is a prescription needed for this?

examples.tl: Uminom ka ng maraming tubig at magpahinga ka.
examples.en: Drink lots of water and rest.

grammar.title: Naka-: body positions and states
grammar.explanation:
The prefix naka- describes the state or position someone is in right now — not an action, just how things currently are: nakaupo (seated), nakatayo (standing), nakahiga (lying down), nakangiti (smiling). You already met one member of this family in Unit 1: nakatira (residing).

These words behave like adjectives: no aspect changes, and they combine with the describing patterns you know. 'Nakahiga si Lola sa sopa' — Grandma is lying on the sofa. 'Nakaupo lang ako buong araw sa trabaho' — I just sit all day at work. 'Bakit ka nakatayo? Umupo ka!' — Why are you standing? Sit down!

Naka- also covers 'wearing/using' states you'll meet more later: nakasalamin (wearing glasses), nakasapatos (wearing shoes). For now, master the position words — doctors use them for instructions too: 'Humiga po kayo' (lie down — the action) versus 'nakahiga' (the resulting state).

examples.tl: Nakahiga pa si Ben. May sakit siya.
examples.en: Ben is still lying down. He's sick.

examples.tl: Nakaupo ako sa harap ng computer buong araw, kaya sumasakit ang likod ko.
examples.en: I sit in front of the computer all day, so my back aches.

examples.tl: Nakatayo lang kami sa dyip; puno na kasi.
examples.en: We just stood in the jeepney; it was already full.

example.tl: Masakit ang buong katawan ko.
example.en: My whole body aches.

example.tl: Masakit ang ulo ko mula kanina.
example.en: My head has been hurting since earlier.

example.tl: Sumakit ang tiyan ko pagkatapos kumain.
example.en: My stomach started hurting after eating.

example.tl: Masakit ang likod ni Tatay.
example.en: Dad's back hurts.

example.tl: Masakit ang lalamunan ko. Hindi ako makakanta.
example.en: My throat hurts. I can't sing.

example.tl: May sirang ngipin ako.
example.en: I have a bad (broken) tooth.

example.tl: Namumula ang mata mo. Okay ka lang ba?
example.en: Your eye is red. Are you okay?

example.tl: Hugasan mo ang mga kamay mo bago kumain.
example.en: Wash your hands before eating.

example.tl: Masakit ang paa ko. Ang layo ng nilakad natin!
example.en: My feet hurt. We walked so far!

example.tl: Sumasakit ang balikat ko sa mabigat na bag.
example.en: My shoulder aches from the heavy bag.

vocab.note: masakit ang X ko = my X hurts

example.tl: Masakit pa rin ba ang tiyan mo?
example.en: Does your stomach still hurt?

example.tl: Sumasakit na naman ang ulo ko.
example.en: My head is aching again.

vocab.note: may sakit = sick; sakit ng ulo = headache

example.tl: May sakit si Ana kaya wala siya ngayon.
example.en: Ana is sick, so she's not here today.

example.tl: Mataas ang lagnat ng bata.
example.en: The child's fever is high.

example.tl: May ubo ako, pero wala akong lagnat.
example.en: I have a cough, but I don't have a fever.

example.tl: May sipon ang lahat sa bahay namin!
example.en: Everyone at our house has a cold!

example.tl: Nahihilo ako. Uupo muna ako.
example.en: I'm dizzy. I'll sit down for a bit.

example.tl: May sugat ang kamay niya.
example.en: His hand has a cut.

vocab.note: Masama ang pakiramdam ko = I feel unwell

example.tl: Kumusta ang pakiramdam mo ngayon?
example.en: How are you feeling now?

example.tl: Kailangan po ng reseta para sa gamot na ito.

vocab.note: tatlong beses sa isang araw = 3x a day

example.tl: Inumin ito tatlong beses sa isang araw.

example.tl: Bumili ako ng gamot sa botika.

example.tl: Nakaupo si Lola sa tabi ng bintana.
example.en: Grandma is seated by the window.

dialogue.title: At the barangay clinic
dialogue.context: Liza has been feeling sick since last night, so she visits the neighborhood clinic and talks to the doctor.

lines.speaker: Doktor
lines.tl: Magandang umaga. Umupo po kayo. Ano po ang nararamdaman ninyo?
lines.en: Good morning. Please have a seat. What are you feeling?

lines.speaker: Liza
lines.tl: Masama po ang pakiramdam ko mula kagabi. Masakit ang ulo ko at ang lalamunan ko.
lines.en: I've been feeling unwell since last night. My head and my throat hurt.

lines.speaker: Liza
lines.tl: Mayroon po, kagabi. May ubo rin po ako at konting sipon.
lines.en: I did last night. I also have a cough and a bit of a cold.

lines.speaker: Liza
lines.tl: Hindi naman po. Pagod lang po siguro. Nakaupo ako sa harap ng computer buong araw.
lines.en: Not really. Maybe just tired. I sit in front of a computer all day.

lines.speaker: Doktor
lines.tl: Sige po. Trangkaso po yata ito. Huwag muna kayong pumasok sa trabaho.
lines.en: Alright. This looks like the flu. Don't go in to work for now.

lines.speaker: Liza
lines.tl: May gamot po ba ako na dapat inumin?
lines.en: Is there medicine I should take?

lines.speaker: Doktor
lines.tl: Oo. Ito ang reseta. Inumin ninyo ang tableta tatlong beses sa isang araw, pagkatapos kumain.
lines.en: Yes. Here's the prescription. Take the tablet three times a day, after meals.

lines.speaker: Liza
lines.tl: Tatlong beses po. Sige po. May bawal po ba?
lines.en: Three times a day. Got it. Is anything not allowed?

lines.speaker: Doktor
lines.tl: Bawal muna ang malamig na inumin. Uminom kayo ng maraming tubig at humiga nang maaga.
lines.en: No cold drinks for now. Drink lots of water and lie down early.

lines.speaker: Doktor
lines.tl: Walang anuman. Magpagaling po kayo! Balikan ninyo ako kung hindi pa kayo magaling sa Biyernes.
lines.en: You're welcome. Get well soon! Come back to me if you're not better by Friday.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'My head hurts'?
exercises.explain: The pattern is masakit ang + body part + ng-form owner: masakit ang ulo ko.

exercises.prompt: ___ lagnat ang anak ko. (My child has a fever.)
exercises.explain: Symptoms you have use A1's may: may lagnat, may ubo, may sipon.

exercises.prompt: 'Sumasakit ang likod ko' differs from 'Masakit ang likod ko' because sumasakit...
choices: describes recurring/ongoing aching (a verb in incompleted aspect)
exercises.explain: Sumasakit is the incompleted form of sumakit — it aches repeatedly or keeps hurting; masakit simply states it's painful.

exercises.prompt: Ano po ang ___ ninyo? (What are you feeling? — the doctor's standard question)
exercises.explain: Nararamdaman (from ramdam, 'feel') is the set phrase: Ano ang nararamdaman mo/ninyo?

exercises.prompt: The pharmacist says: 'Inumin po ninyo ito dalawang beses sa isang araw.' What are the instructions?
choices: Take it once every two days
Drink two glasses of water daily
exercises.explain: Dalawang beses sa isang araw = two times in one day. Inumin is the object-focus command 'take/drink it.'

exercises.tl: Masakit ang lalamunan ko at may ubo ako, pero wala akong lagnat.
exercises.prompt: Which symptoms does the speaker have?
choices: Sore throat and cough, no fever
Cough and fever, no sore throat
exercises.explain: Masakit ang lalamunan (sore throat), may ubo (cough), wala akong lagnat (no fever).

exercises.prompt: Which word describes someone who is lying down (the state, not the action)?
exercises.explain: Naka- forms describe current states: nakahiga = in a lying position. Humiga is the action verb 'to lie down.'

exercises.prompt: ___ si Lola sa sopa. Natutulog yata siya. (Grandma is lying on the sofa.)
exercises.explain: The naka- stative nakahiga describes her position; no aspect marking needed.

exercises.prompt: Do you have medicine for a cough?
exercises.answer: May gamot po ba kayo para sa ubo?
accept: May gamot po ba kayo para sa ubo
May gamot ba kayo para sa ubo
Mayroon po ba kayong gamot para sa ubo
exercises.explain: May + ba for the yes/no question, and para sa marks what the medicine is for.

exercises.prompt: Huwag muna kayong pumasok sa trabaho. Magpahinga po kayo.
exercises.answer: Don't go in to work for now. Please rest.
accept: Don't go in to work for now. Please rest
Don't go to work for now. Rest
For now don't go to work. Get some rest
exercises.explain: Huwag muna = don't (for now); pumasok sa trabaho = go in to work; magpahinga = rest.

exercises.prompt: The doctor says 'Humiga po kayo.' What should the patient do?
exercises.explain: Humiga is the action verb 'lie down' in command form; nakahiga would describe the resulting state.

exercises.prompt: My stomach started hurting after eating.
exercises.answer: Sumakit ang tiyan ko pagkatapos kumain.
accept: Sumakit ang tiyan ko pagkatapos kumain
Pagkatapos kumain, sumakit ang tiyan ko
Sumakit ang tiyan ko pagkatapos akong kumain
exercises.explain: Completed sumakit for the onset of pain; pagkatapos kumain from Unit 3 gives 'after eating.'

exercises.prompt: Gumaling ka na ba? — Oo, wala ___ akong lagnat. (Yes, my fever is gone.)
exercises.explain: Wala na = no longer there; the particle na from Unit 5 marks the change of state.

exercises.tl: Inumin ninyo ang gamot tatlong beses sa isang araw, pagkatapos kumain. Bawal muna ang kape.
exercises.prompt: What is one instruction the pharmacist gives?
exercises.explain: Bawal muna ang kape = coffee is off-limits for now. The medicine is three times a day, after meals.
